ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the figure is a common wire; on the left is a voltage source labeled 2V, with polarity positive at the top and negative at the bottom; on the right is a voltage source labeled 1V, with polarity also positive at the top and negative at the bottom; the top-left node is connected through a 2Ω resistor to the top middle/right node; in the middle there is a 1Ω resistor connected from this top node to the bottom common wire. Reasoning: Take the bottom common wire as the reference node 0V. The left voltage source makes the node voltage at the left end of the 2Ω resistor be +2V; the right voltage source makes the node voltage at the right end of the 2Ω resistor, that is, the node connected to the upper end of the 1Ω resistor, be +1V. Therefore the voltage across the 2Ω resistor is 2V - 1V = 1V. Its power P = V^2/R = 1^2/2 = 0.5W.
